issues.legal_issue: Relevant facts concerning an accused’s subsequent criminal conduct must be disclosed to the court deciding a bail application.
Bail parity does not justify granting bail when the other accused have distinguishable roles and criminal conduct.
Prolonged incarceration does not entitle accused persons to bail when their subsequent conduct weighs against release.
Bail may be cancelled for some accused based on their subsequent conduct while bail is maintained for a co-accused not implicated in that conduct.
